slides.title: Executive Audiences Need a Different Style
bullets: Scientific conversations with a KOL allow technical depth and a progressive build-up
A steering committee or senior leadership needs synthesis and immediate clarity
Time and attention are limited, so the format has to change

slides.title: Start With the Conclusion
bullets: Lead with the main message and the decision or action expected, in the first seconds
This inverts the usual scientific narrative that builds toward a conclusion
This synthesis discipline doesn't come naturally to many technically strong professionals

slides.title: Strategic Relevance Over Operational Detail
bullets: Leadership needs the implications for their decisions, not every step of the process
Translate detailed field work into the language of impact and decision
Keep the underlying rigor while cutting irrelevant detail

slides.title: Disciplined Use of Visual Aids
bullets: Simple charts or diagrams communicate at a glance what a paragraph would take to explain
Avoid overloading a single slide or page with information
This is a common gap for professionals used to dense academic publications

slides.title: Synthesis Without Sacrificing Rigor
bullets: Synthesis does not mean simplifying until precision is lost
Relevant limitations of evidence or a recommendation still need to be surfaced
Select what's essential for the decision, but never sacrifice scientific honesty

slides.title: Practice It Deliberately
bullets: Actively seek opportunities to present to leadership audiences
Ask for specific feedback on clarity and synthesis
Critically review your own presentations before delivering them

takeaway.title: Executive communication trades narrative build-up for immediate, rigorous synthesis
bullets: Start with the conclusion and the decision needed, not the supporting detail
Translate field work into impact and decision language without losing rigor
Deliberate practice with real leadership audiences is what builds this skill
